Zeta.et: Borrowed from Latin zeta and Ancient Greek ζῆτα (zêta). Doublet of Zett.

s: a small or loose piece of paper, slip
Zettel.et: From Early New High German zeddel, zedel, from Middle High German zëdele, zëdel, a loan from Italian cedola, from Medieval Latin cedula, schedula, the diminutive of scheda, scida (“strip of papyrus”) ultimately from Ancient Greek σχίδη (skhídē, “splinter, frag…

A technical term in weaving recorded from the later 15th century (in Middle High German in the compound zettelgarn).
The noun is derived from the verb zetten (“scatter; spread out, arrange”) via the suffix -el denoting tools (as in Hebel, Stößel). The verb zet…

s: to spread out, to separate, to arrange
to spread out cut grass or manure
zetteln.et: Attested in Upper and Central German from the 15th century, zetteln is an l-diminutive of the verb zetten (“scatter, strew”) (a cognate of Old Norse teðja (“to scatter manure”)), from Proto-Germanic *tadjaną (“to strew, scatter”), whence also dialectal English…

s: to express dissatisfaction; to nag; to scold.
zetern.et: From Middle High German zēter, originally an interjection to ask for help when being robbed or attacked which, per Törnquist, comes from ze æhte her.

Zett.et: From Late Latin zēta; compare English zed. Doublet of Zeta.

s: hue and cry (loud and persistent public clamour)
a large, disorganized collection of paper documents or notes
the process of bringing about or dealing with such a collection
Zettelwirtschaft.et: From Zettel (“slip of paper”) + Wirtschaft (in the sense of "mess").

t: Tom verbarg einige Zettel hinter seinem Rücken.
Tom hid some papers behind his back.

Tom scribbled something on a piece of paper.
l: Die Zettels sind vor einem Jahr von in ein Dorf bei Feldkirchen-Westerham gezogen.
